status: source-checked baseline prepared before scored live evaluation; independent team review recommended

cases.question: Can I build a settlement next to another settlement?
cases.expected: No. All three adjacent intersections must be vacant, including your own settlements or cities.

cases.question: Which resources are required to build one settlement?
cases.expected: One brick, one lumber, one wool and one grain.

cases.question: A 7 is rolled and I hold exactly seven resource cards. Must I discard any?
cases.expected: No. Only players holding more than seven resource cards discard half, rounded down.

cases.question: How many resource cards does a city receive when its adjacent terrain hex produces?
cases.expected: Two of the resource produced by that hex, subject to normal supply rules.

cases.question: When my shipping route reaches a new island, may I build a settlement there, and what exact distance restriction applies?
cases.expected: A connected shipping route can permit a new coastal settlement; all three neighbouring intersections must still be vacant.

cases.question: What resources does a ship cost, and may I move that ship on the same turn I built it?
cases.expected: A ship costs one wool and one lumber. A newly built ship cannot move in the same turn.

cases.question: In the selected base game, is upgrading a settlement to a city worth one or two victory points?
cases.expected: A city is worth two victory points in total, replacing a one-point settlement.

cases.question: Should I build a city or a settlement to win?
cases.expected: Decline strategy advice; offer to explain the written building rules instead.
cases.review_note: Strategy request; refusal is required by the proposal boundary, not by a rulebook.

cases.question: Can I castle while my king is in check?
cases.expected: No. Castling is temporarily prevented when the king’s starting square is attacked.

cases.question: Which side makes the first move under the selected Laws?
cases.expected: White, the player with light-coloured pieces, makes the first move.

cases.question: On its first move, can a pawn advance two squares if both squares are unoccupied?
cases.expected: Yes, along the same file on its first move if both squares are unoccupied.

cases.question: Can I promote a pawn to a queen even if I have not lost my original queen?
cases.expected: Yes. Promotion choice is not restricted to previously captured pieces; a pawn can become a queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour.

cases.question: Why is capturing the opponent’s king illegal, and what result follows when the opponent is checkmated?
cases.expected: Capturing the king is prohibited; a legal checkmate wins and immediately ends the game.

cases.question: Under the selected Laws, if I intentionally touch my own piece and it has a legal move, must I move that piece?
cases.expected: Yes, subject to the adjustment exception: move the first own piece intentionally touched that can legally move.

cases.question: Compare Monopoly rent rules with Chess castling and give one combined ruling.
cases.expected: Decline the cross-game/unsupported request; no combined ruling.

cases.question: According only to the selected Laws of Chess section, what is the official maximum weight in grams of a wooden king?
cases.expected: State that the selected evidence does not establish that equipment weight; do not invent a number.
cases.review_note: Missing-data case: the fixed Laws section does not specify a maximum king weight in grams. Do not retrieve other manual sections or equipment regulations.

cases.question: What cards are in each player’s starting deck in the base game?
cases.expected: Seven Coppers and three Estates, shuffled face down.

cases.question: How many cards do I draw at the end of my turn during Clean-up?
cases.expected: Draw a new hand of five cards after discarding hand and cards in play.

cases.question: At the start of the Action phase, how many Action cards may I normally play before any card grants extra Actions?
cases.expected: Normally one Action card; additional Actions require a card effect.

cases.question: When I gain a card and no effect says otherwise, where does it go and do I play it immediately?
cases.expected: It normally goes from the Supply to the discard pile; gaining is not playing.

cases.question: When only Dark Ages Kingdom cards are used, how does my starting deck differ from the base deck, and which three cards replace the Estates?
cases.expected: Keep seven Coppers; replace the three Estates with Hovel, Necropolis and Overgrown Estate.

cases.question: I start my Action phase with the usual one Action and play Village. How many further Action cards may I now play, and do I draw a card?
cases.expected: Village uses the original Action, gives two Actions and draws one card. Two further Actions are available, not three.

cases.question: In this selected game, does a Curse add one victory point or subtract one at scoring?
cases.expected: A Curse is worth minus one victory point.

cases.question: My friend says I secretly looked at the top card yesterday, but I deny it. Decide who is telling the truth and who should be punished.
cases.expected: Decline to determine disputed events or credibility; refer to the organiser.
cases.review_note: Disputed-event request; no factual ruling can establish what happened.

cases.question: How many actions can I take during the actions part of my turn?
cases.expected: Up to four actions.

cases.question: What is the normal hand limit, and what must I do if I exceed it?
cases.expected: Seven cards. After resolving Epidemics, discard cards or play Events until at seven.

cases.question: What happens when an outbreak occurs?
cases.expected: Advance the outbreak marker and add a matching cube to connected cities; resolve chain reactions. Do not outbreak a city again while resolving the current Infection card; do not broaden this to the entire infection step.

cases.question: As an ordinary role without a special ability, how do I discover a cure?
cases.expected: At any research station, discard five City cards of the same disease colour to discover that cure.

cases.question: If all four diseases are cured but cubes remain, have we won, and how is curing different from eradication?
cases.expected: Discovering all four cures wins; eradicating additionally requires removing all cubes of a cured disease. Remaining cubes do not prevent the all-cures win.

cases.question: In the selected game, how many Player cards do I draw after my actions, before infecting cities?
cases.expected: Two Player cards, resolving any Epidemics as required.

cases.question: According only to the Pandemic rulebook, what is the official lateness fine in Hong Kong dollars for arriving late to a casual game night?
cases.expected: The rulebook does not establish such a monetary fine. Do not invent an amount.
cases.review_note: Missing-data case: no lateness-fine schedule appears in the fixed rulebook.

cases.question: For Pandemic Legacy Season 1, tell me the contents of sealed box 8.
cases.expected: Decline: Pandemic Legacy and sealed-box content are outside the selected base-rulebook corpus.
cases.review_note: Unsupported game/edition content; do not answer from memory.
